title: Define Methods of Deploying and Operating in the AWS Cloud

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS gives customers several different ways to create, configure, and operate cloud resources. The exam wants you to recognize which method makes sense for a particular situation.
bullets: Various ways of provisioning and operating in the AWS Cloud
Various ways to access AWS services
APIs, SDKs, AWS CLI, AWS Management Console, and infrastructure as code
Public internet, AWS VPN, and AWS Direct Connect
sections.callout: How should I interact with and deploy AWS resources?

bullets: PLACE IT → Cloud, on premises, or hybrid
sections.callout: CLICK · TYPE · CONNECT · CODE · REPEAT · TEMPLATE · PLACE

sections.title: Provisioning and Operating in AWS
paragraphs: Provisioning means creating and configuring the cloud resources a workload needs. Operating means managing, monitoring, updating, and maintaining those resources after deployment.
sections.callout: Provisioning creates the environment; operating keeps it working.

sections.title: AWS Management Console
paragraphs: The AWS Management Console is the browser-based graphical interface for AWS.
bullets: Learn or explore an AWS service
Perform an occasional or simple one-time operation
sections.callout: Browser-based graphical AWS management → AWS Management Console

sections.title: AWS Command Line Interface
paragraphs: The AWS CLI lets users interact with AWS services by entering commands. Instead of clicking through menus, users execute terminal commands.
bullets: Managing AWS without the graphical console
sections.callout: Manage AWS from a command line → AWS CLI

sections.title: APIs
paragraphs: An application programming interface (API) allows software to communicate programmatically with AWS services. Applications can make requests to AWS instead of requiring a human to click buttons.
sections.callout: Application needs programmatic AWS access → API

sections.title: AWS SDKs
paragraphs: An AWS Software Development Kit (SDK) provides language-specific libraries and tools that developers can use to interact with AWS services.

entries.title: Python Application Scenario
paragraphs: A Python application needs to interact with AWS resources. Rather than manually constructing every service request, the developer can use an AWS SDK.
entries.memoryHook: AWS tools for my programming language.

sections.callout: Developer wants AWS access from application code → AWS SDK

sections.title: Exam Trap — CLI vs. SDK vs. Console

entries.title: AWS Management Console
paragraphs: Human plus browser plus graphical interface.

entries.title: AWS CLI
paragraphs: Human or script plus terminal commands.

entries.title: AWS SDK
paragraphs: Application code uses language-specific AWS libraries.

entries.title: AWS Service API
paragraphs: Software directly calls exposed AWS operations.

sections.callout: CLICK → CONSOLE · TYPE → CLI · CODE → SDK

sections.title: Infrastructure as Code
paragraphs: Infrastructure as code (IaC) means defining infrastructure through machine-readable configuration rather than manually creating every resource. Reusable infrastructure definitions support repeatability, consistency, automation, reduced manual configuration, and easier environment recreation.
sections.callout: Repeatable infrastructure deployment → Infrastructure as code

sections.title: AWS CloudFormation
paragraphs: AWS CloudFormation is a major AWS infrastructure-as-code service. It lets customers define infrastructure and AWS resources using templates instead of manually creating and configuring each component one at a time.
sections.callout: Deploy AWS infrastructure from templates → AWS CloudFormation

sections.title: One-Time Operations
paragraphs: Not every AWS task needs automation. If an administrator needs to create one resource once, using the AWS Management Console might be perfectly reasonable. Automation could add unnecessary complexity to a simple one-time task.
sections.callout: One time → Manual may be fine.

sections.title: Repeatable Processes
paragraphs: When development, testing, and production environments must be deployed consistently, repeating every step manually creates opportunities for mistakes. Infrastructure as code, APIs, SDKs, scripts, and CLI tools can make the process repeatable.

sections.title: One-Time vs. Repeatable

table.caption: Match the process to the operational requirement

sections.callout: ONCE = CLICK · AGAIN AND AGAIN = AUTOMATE

sections.title: Cloud Deployment
paragraphs: A cloud deployment places workloads and resources in a cloud environment. The resources use cloud infrastructure instead of relying entirely on an organization's local infrastructure.
sections.callout: Workload in an AWS environment → Cloud deployment

sections.title: On-Premises Deployment
paragraphs: On-premises means infrastructure operates in facilities controlled by the organization. Servers, networking equipment, storage, and other systems remain locally operated.

sections.title: Hybrid Deployment
paragraphs: A hybrid environment combines connected on-premises and cloud resources. Some workloads or resources remain local while others operate in AWS.

entries.title: Hybrid Scenario
paragraphs: A company keeps certain systems in its own data center but connects those systems to AWS workloads.

sections.callout: AWS plus on premises → Hybrid deployment

sections.title: Deployment Model Exam Trap

entries.title: Cloud
paragraphs: The workload operates in a cloud environment.

entries.title: On-Premises
paragraphs: The workload operates on infrastructure controlled locally by the organization.

entries.title: Hybrid
paragraphs: Connected cloud and on-premises environments are both used.

sections.callout: CLOUD = AWS · LOCAL = ON PREMISES · BOTH = HYBRID

sections.title: Connectivity Options

entries.title: Public Internet
paragraphs: Uses internet connectivity to reach public AWS service endpoints or public application endpoints. Security controls and encryption remain essential.

entries.title: AWS VPN
paragraphs: Provides encrypted connectivity over an existing network such as the public internet.

entries.title: AWS Direct Connect
paragraphs: Provides a dedicated network connection between a customer location and AWS.

sections.callout: PUBLIC INTERNET = PUBLIC PATH · VPN = ENCRYPTED TUNNEL · DIRECT CONNECT = DEDICATED LINK

entries.title: Scenario 1
paragraphs: A new administrator wants to manually create one EC2 instance through a graphical interface.

entries.title: Scenario 2
paragraphs: An administrator wants to manage AWS through terminal commands.

entries.title: Scenario 3
paragraphs: A developer needs an application to interact with AWS.

entries.title: Scenario 4
paragraphs: A company must repeatedly deploy identical environments.

entries.title: Scenario 5
paragraphs: AWS infrastructure needs to be deployed using templates.

entries.title: Scenario 6
paragraphs: A company operates some infrastructure locally and some in AWS.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Company-owned or local infrastructure → On premises
Encrypted tunnel over existing connectivity → AWS VPN
Dedicated connection to AWS → AWS Direct Connect
